cells.tense: You are seeing the machinery under the thing and it satisfies you to see it.
cells.ask: Tell one person the shape you noticed, as if they could use it, and let that be the whole of what you wanted from saying it.
cells.core:
You can see the pattern under something and that's enough on its own. Not the facts of it — the way it works, the joints and levers showing, the surface gone. This kind of sight usually arrives late, after wanting it has stopped being urgent. What you imagined has been felt through, so there's a fullness to it now, not a hunger.

You're not waiting to be satisfied and you're not gripping it either. This is a good place to stand, and it costs something to keep standing here: it means letting the picture stay partial and still letting it be finished. So say the shape out loud once, as a thing someone could pick up and use. Not to prove you saw it. Because a pattern spoken to another person gets clearer, and you get to find out whether it holds.
cells.sheetLine: You see how it works, and that's enough.
cells.verb: Imagining it fully and feeling every bit of it until it multiplies
cells.place: At the bare pattern under a thing, where the mechanism shows and the detail drops away

cells.tense: You are reaching for a satisfaction that is still somewhere ahead of you to arrive.
cells.ask: Pick one thing already in front of you and put twenty quiet minutes into it exactly as it is, then stop before you improve it.
cells.core:
You're already imagining the finished shape and the finished feeling with it, and the version in front of you loses by comparison. So you keep reaching — a better pattern, a cleaner version, the one that will finally land right. The abundance you're chasing gets further the harder you reach, because you're measuring the present against a picture that hasn't happened.

What helps here isn't less vision. It's tending something that already exists, at the size it actually is, without hauling it toward the future. That's the part that doesn't exhaust you, once you quit trying to arrive. Choose one real thing and give it twenty quiet minutes as it is. Then stop. Quitting there is what shows you the difference between caring for it and forcing it.

cells.verb: Imagining it fully and feeling every bit of it until it multiplies

cells.tense: You stopped saying what you could see and you are still standing in the place where you stopped.
cells.ask: Write one sentence about how something works, keep it a day without deciding if it's right, and read it back the next morning.
cells.core:
You can read the pattern under a thing — the joints, the way it moves — and you've stopped putting it anywhere. Whatever put the brake on is behind you now, but the pen's still down and you're standing there. What you can see hasn't gone. The saying has.

Not-knowing isn't the problem here; being at ease inside it is what lets a perception land without a fight. Start smaller than feels reasonable: one sentence about how something works, held for a day without judging it, read back the next morning. The pattern under a thing shows itself to someone willing to hold it quietly. That's a small move, and it's enough to get you writing again on the strength of what you actually know.
cells.sheetLine: You can see it and you've stopped saying it.
cells.verb: Imagining it fully and feeling every bit of it until it multiplies

cells.tense: You are reading the pattern and calling it something that simply turned up on its own.
cells.ask: Write one line about a pattern you caught this week, as yours, somewhere you can see it written.
cells.core:
You're already reading the pattern under things — noticing how a situation is built, where the seams are, what makes it move. That reading is happening daily. But when you talk about it, it sounds like the insight arrived on its own, or the situation simply showed itself. Your hand is on that, and the hand isn't being counted.

The work is to take the claim back down to its smaller form: one pattern, one line, owned. That's the honest size of it, and it's the practice that keeps the reading accurate instead of restless. Pick one pattern you caught this week. Say it as yours, once, somewhere you can see it written. Not as a boast — as a fact about who actually caught it.
cells.sheetLine: You read the pattern. You talk like it read itself.
cells.verb: Imagining it fully and feeling every bit of it until it multiplies

attempts.check: The unsupported claim is that the person has been treating the abundance as still on its way — the record only gives a status, not a history. The reader could reasonably say the shortage is real and not just a delay, so the ask must stand as a plain next act and not a correction of their account. The ask does survive being wrong: writing down what is already there teaches something either way. The sentence that serves the writer is 'the abundance is already here' — cut it, because it tells the person what their own eyes are for.
